hints: Think about how you add 1 on paper. Where do you start, and when can you stop early?

Walk the digits array from the last position with a carry. A digit below 9 just increases and you are done; a 9 becomes 0 and the carry moves left. If every digit was 9, the result needs one extra leading 1, so it is one element longer.

1. Start at the last index.
  2. If digits[i] < 9: increase it and return the array.
  3. Otherwise set digits[i] = 0 and move one step left.
  4. If you run off the front, all digits were 9: return a new array of length + 1 with a 1 in front and zeros after it.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Turn the digits into a number, add 1, split it back. Fails in Java because 1000 digits overflow every built-in number type.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Add 1 directly on the digit array from right to left, carrying only through trailing 9s.
approaches.space: O(1) extra (O(n) only when all digits are 9)

explain: For [1,2,9]: the last digit is 9, so it becomes 0 and we carry; the middle 2 becomes 3 and the carry stops, giving [1,3,0]. Only trailing 9s are ever changed, which is why we can return at the first digit below 9. The edge case is all 9s (e.g. [9,9]), where every digit becomes 0 and a new leading 1 appears, so the returned array [1,0,0] is one longer than the input.
recognize: "A big number given as an array of digits, do arithmetic" → simulate school arithmetic with a carry from the right.
